full_judgment:
3. At this stage the petitioner Zyta Garments Ltd made an application under Order I rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for impleading it as a party in the suit on the ground that the LCs were actually established by it with the defendant National Bank Ltd in favour of ENAR (Pvt) Ltd Karachi, Pakistan, for supply of fabrics but the supplier failed to supply fabrics on time and when supplied, it supplied inferior quality fabrics. It apprehends that If a decree is passed the money under the decree will be debited from the petitioner's account causing it to suffer irreparable loss and injury. Therefore, it is a necessary and proper party to be added. The application was opposed by the plaintiff respondent Union Bank Ltd and the learned Subordinate Judge rejected the petitioner's prayer to be added as a party on the ground that if it was made a party it would create unnecessary complications in the disposal of the suit. 

 5. The learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the most important party in the contract. If any question is raised by the parties concerned it can only be answered by the petitioner. By not being added as a party it has been highly prejudiced and deprived of an opportunity of being heard. Moreover, if the respondent gets a decree, the decreetal amount will be paid by debiting the account of the petitioner and thus it will suffer irreparable loss and injury only because it was not given an opportunity of being heard by impleading it as a party to the suit.
